axes.model_access: Multi-model aggregation (the consumer answer engine offers several models, official product surface) + enterprise-side retrieval infrastructure (the ARI/Research API line — the official current main-axis narrative).
axes.runtime: Web (you.com) consumer side + API enterprise side; retrieval and generation on the vendor's cloud.
axes.local_files: Conversation history stored on the account-side cloud; no officially stated local data surface or offline mode seen (not verified item by item).
axes.background: Q&A is instant; the enterprise-side Research API is a service surface; no "keep-running-after-shutdown" concept.
axes.tools: Consumer side: answer engine + model switching + apps line (seen on the official site); **enterprise side: Agentic Retrieval (ARI)/Research API is the current main axis** (the official framing has pivoted to enterprise search infrastructure — this dossier is written to the official current framing).
axes.context: Consumer side organized by threads; the enterprise side has no memory concept (API); cross-session memory not verified to an official statement.
axes.permissions: Account + subscription (consumer) / contract (enterprise) (D9: pricing not collected); the training-use switch not verified item by item; **the product's center of gravity has shifted from consumer to enterprise** — the uncertainty of consumer-side investment must be honestly noted.
axes.fit: Fits: enterprise retrieval-infrastructure procurement evaluation (ARI/Research API), consumer-side multi-model switching experience. Does not fit: treating the consumer side as a long-term commitment (the center of gravity has moved to enterprise), mainland direct connection (measured 000).
